# Draft:Jacqui (The Walking Dead)

Jacqui is a fictional character appearing in AMC's The Walking Dead, portrayed Jeryl Prescott and created by Frank Darabont. The character appeared as a major recurring character in the first season of the show, and is one of the first characters to appear without a comic book counterpart.
In the show, Jacqui is one of the first people Rick Grimes encounters after escaping from the tank in Atlanta, Georgia, in the episode "Guts". She displays a great sense of awareness and resourcefulness, who has vast knowledge of the city's layout. After their group is overrun with walkers, Jacqui travels to the CDC with her fellow survivors, only to commit suicide once the building is set to explode, opting to stay inside while her friends flee to safety. Prescott returned as a guest star in the season three episode "Hounded", where she interrogates Rick in one of his hallucinations.
Jacqui had a small role in the television series, but played a pivotal part in the show's first season and earlier storylines. The character has been well-received by television critics, who often comment on the character's loss of potential after her death. Critics also note Jacqui to be one of the series' first major character deaths, after Amy Harrison.
Concept and creation
Jeryl Prescott was cast as the character of Jacqui in 2010. The character was originally planned to only be in two episodes, but was later developed into a full-season character after Darabont reviewed her audition tape, further extending Jacqui's storyline. Although her character does not appear in the original source material, Prescott was already familiar to the comic book series prior to filming the first season.
According to showrunner Frank Darabont, he began a personal dilemma about whether or not he wanted Jacqui to die in the first season, according to actress Jeryl Prescott. "[He] was going back and forth about whether or not he wanted Jacqui to die. There were three possibilities as I recall: that Jacqui would not die; that Jacqui would die, but she would die at the top of season 2; or that Jacqui would just die in the explosion at the end of season 1." Prescott mentioned  that "it's nice to be the only one to go in such a flame of glory. People always want to talk about it because they keep putting themselves in Jacqui's position, wondering if they would reach their point of surrender."
In 2011, it was rumored that Prescott would be returning to season 2 of The Walking Dead, which was quickly debunked. However, she teased the possibility of returning, which would later be in the season three episode "Hounded".
Prescott was a series regular on the show for five episodes in season one, and returned in the form of a guest role in season three. Archive footage of Prescott as Jacqui is present in the season seven episode "The Day Will Come When You Won't Be".
Overview
Season 1
Jacqui makes her debut in the episode "Guts", where she and her group are taking refuge in an abandoned department store, alongside Andrea, Morales, T-Dog, Merle, and Glenn. When Rick finds himself trapped in a nearby tank, Glenn escorts him away from the zombie herd and into the nearby building he and his group are joined at. Once they make it inside the store, Andrea points her gun at Rick, as Jacqui and Morales convince her to put it away. Afterwards, Merle can be heard on the roof shooting a rifle at the dead, which causes the survivors to run up and stop him. On the roof, Merle becomes violent with T-Dog, knocking him to the ground, with Jacqui running to his aid. Merle begins to declare himself as the group's leader, to which Jacqui responds by flipping him off. As the group tries to find a way out, Jacqui reveals that there is a sewer system connected the building, revealing that that she worked for the city's zoning department before the outbreak. This prompts Glenn and Morales to check out the sewers, but to no avail. Rick eventually comes up with a plan to escape, by disguising themselves as the dead by rubbing their blood on their clothes. Jacqui assists Glenn and Rick by covering their coats in the blood, which allows them to blend in with the zombies and acquire a vehicle. With Glenn distracting the herd and Rick making his way back to the department store, Jacqui and the others hop into the truck, leaving behind a handcuffed Merle and heading back to their camp.
In the episode "Tell It to the Frogs", Jacqui and the group return to the camp. In the following day, she assists in daily chores, and begins to enjoy a conversation with the women of the camp. She reveals that the pre-apocalypse item she misses the most is her "coffee maker with a dual drip filter and grinder". When Ed Peletier begins to approach the group, Jacqui the first to defend his wife against her husband's abusive behavior. As he begins to walk away with Carol, Jacqui tries to help her, only for Carol to be punched in the face by her husband, which causes Shane to beat him up in return, which Jacqui watches.
In "Vatos", Jacqui congratulates Andrea and Amy on their fishing expedition, which they cook and serve at the campfire later that night. During so, Jacqui joins in, mentioning that the world has ended in response to Dale's comments. Afterwards, this prompts Dale to tell a story about his watch and the irony of time. Shortly after, the camp is overrun with zombies, which results in the deaths of nearly every member of the camp. Jacqui is one of the members who defends their camp, and survives. The episode ends with Jacqui and the rest of the survivors acknowledging Jim's dream and the corpses that surround them.
In the episode "Wildfire", Jacqui assists in burying their friends and burning the corpses of zombies. While doing so, she notices Jim is wounded, and begins to question if he has been bitten. Jim begs her not to tell anyone, but Jacqui immediately alerts the camp that he is infected, causing them to isolate Jim from the rest of the group. Before the group departs for the CDC, Jacqui says her goodbyes to Morales and his family. On the road, Jacqui sits on the bed in Dale's RV with Jim, tending to his illness. Before they make it, the RV breaks down, and Jacqui alerts the group that Jim's infection has gotten worse. He decides to stay behind, with Jacqui tearfully giving him a kiss and saying her goodbye as the group departs. At the CDC, Jacqui and the group fight their way to the entrance, only to be denied access by Edwin Jenner. He reluctantly decides to open the doors, allowing the group to enter.
In the sixth episode "TS-19", the group is given access to Edwin's bunker in the CDC, who reveals that they can stay for as long as they want. He directs the group to the showers, where Jacqui and the rest of her group clean themselves. They eventually all join for dinner, reminiscing on their triumphs and the people that they have lost. Later, Jenner reveals to the group the effects of the disease, showcasing his wife (the subject) on archive footage and how the infection spreads. He then points out the clock counting down, revealing that the building is set to explode, and the group is locked inside. Rick and the group begin to demand letting them out, but Jenner refuses. He is eventually convinced to open the doors, and the group makes a run for it. Jacqui reveals to her friends that she does not want to end up like Jim or Amy, and opts to stay behind and commit suicide. Moments after the group departs, Jacqui and Edwin Jenner are killed in the explosion.
Season 3
In the episode "Hounded", Rick is traumatized by the death of his wife, Lori Grimes. During this time, he receives four phone calls, the third being a woman who demands to know "why" he didn't tell the previous man how his wife died. She begins to call Rick by his name, and states that show knows him, and hangs up the phone. On the fourth call, the voice reveals herself to be Lori, and that the previous calls were from Amy, Jim, and Jacqui (who was the third call). Rick then comes to the realization that he is hallucinating, and listens to Lori over the phone.
Season 7
In the episode "The Day Will Come When You Won't Be", Jacqui is briefly seen by Rick in several flashbacks as he recalls memories of his friends after Negan kills Glenn and Abraham.
Reception
The character of Jacqui has been well-received by television credits. Her character in the show is often cited as wasted potential, after Jacqui commits suicide at the CDC. Faith Roswell for Screen Rant mentioned the "Architect Had The Potential To Be An Asset To Later Walking Dead Seasons," further writing that Jacqui "is the exact kind of obscure character who could have improved The Walking Dead if she'd survived longer. The quiet, kind and introverted Jacqui established herself as an asset in the early days of the apocalypse. As an architect, Jacqui's knowledge of the city buildings had the potential to help the group escape a department store. Though the plan didn't work, Jacqui's expertise could have been valuable in later seasons of The Walking Dead when the groups were creating new settlements [...] an architect like Jacqui could have become a vital character, especially during season 6 after Alexandria was overrun. Jacqui lost hope early, choosing to die when Jenner's laboratory exploded. Her decision was a shocking and emotional moment in The Walking Dead. However, it was also a case of wasted potential, as Jacqui could perhaps have regained her hope by having a key role in rebuilding society." Jenna Scott for Collider also commented on the Jacqui's death, mentioning that "Her actions are nothing short of courageous and encapsulate her entire character arc. Like Dale, Jacqui refuses to let the outbreak change her morals."
Saim Cheeda for Screen Rant mentioned Jacqui in his list of "The Walking Dead's 10 Most Forgettable Characters, According To Reddit", writing: "Jenner had taken the liberty to blow up the CDC against everyone’s wishes, eventually allowing them to leave if they wanted to. Jacqui had been a fighter before that, yet decided to stay and perish without any setup for this decision. The Walking Dead has changed so much since Season 1 that Jacqui’s now just a footnote to the story that few deem worth remembering."
Marc Kleinhenz commented positively on the character, mentioning her in his list of "The Walking Dead: 15 Most Interesting Recurring Characters", stating that "[Jacqui] does represent something that the show hasn’t depicted too often in its six-year run: defeat. Rather than face the intolerable, interminable period of time before the government can reassert control over what used to be the country (if, indeed, it ever does), she opts for suicide, being incinerated in the Center for Disease Control’s self-destruction. It’s an interesting variation on the theme, and it makes for one memorable scene – and how many of the recurring characters can lay claim to that feat?"
In popular culture
For Entertainment Weekly, Jeryl Prescott Sales was invited to take part in a photoshoot for former The Walking Dead stars who play currently-deceased characters. She was joined alongside Emily Kinney, Chad L. Coleman, and some of her former co-stars, including Madison Lintz (Sophia Peletier) and IronE Singelton (T-Dog).
